To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the real world CO2 and NOX performance of a Euro 6 diesel passenger car is significantly worse than its respective WLTC emissions, while the real world NOX performance of an Euro 6 gasoline/CNG bi fuel passenger car is significantly better than its respective WLTP emissions.

- The WLTC, with realistic road load, is a suitable test cycle for the assessment of the environmental performance of passenger cars, under real world driving conditions, in terms of both CO2 and NO emissions.
• The real world CO2 emissions are higher than the WLTC ones.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the assessment of the environmental performance of two Euro 5 passenger cars, one equipped with a common-rail diesel engine and the other with a bi fuel gasoline/ compressed natural gas (CNG) one.
the real world assessment of the environmental performance of two Euro 5 passenger cars, one diesel and one gasoline, equipped with a Three Way Catalyst (TCW).
the assessment of the emissions of two Euro 4 vehicles during real world driving and laboratory testing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bi fuel vehicle is the most environmentally friendly one, in all the driving conditions, while the diesel vehicle exhibits the worst NOx emissions, but also the lowest fuel consumption.
, in the case of the two cars tested, natural gas is an excellent alternative to gasoline, while it is a good alternative to diesel.
, for both vehicles, the real world NOx emissions were higher than the WLTC levels, and the bi fuel car is a very promising solution for the reduction of NOx emissions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the real world emissions of both vehicles were in line with their laboratory performance.
the WLTC is a useful tool to assess the environmental performance of vehicles, but the RDE compliant driving route is more representative of real world driving.
both cars exhibited very good environmental performance under all driving conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the WLTC does not fully represent the real world emissions of the tested cars, and the RDE test schedule should be used for the evaluation of the real world performance of the vehicles, in terms of emissions.
the real driving emissions of a vehicle are highly influenced by the driving style.
the RDE compliant test route can provide a realistic and representative picture of the emissions performance of modern Euro 6 vehicles under real world conditions.
